AGENDA

  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, iOS and
Android devices using a free app called Cablecast and choosing "Glendale TV" from the menu.
Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Asatryan directed staff to post the agenda forecast on the city’s website to
  make it available to the public. Kassakhian seconded. Councilmember Asatryan asked that
  the motions in the minutes include the specific directions given by councilmembers. City
  Attorney Garcia stated that when there is a motion to note and file with additional directions
  from Council, those directions are not usually included in the motion as conditions. He asked
  that if there is a specific direction that Council would like to include as a condition of that
  motion, that they make that direction explicit.

  Councilmember Devine announced that Glenn Webb, an environmental and sustainability
  advocate, passed away. She sent her condolences to the family of the deceased.

  Mayor Brotman spoke about the catastrophic loss and ethnic cleansing of Armenians by the
  Azerbaijani government from the Republic of Artsakh. He stated that we should be thinking
  about asking our government to put sanctions on Azerbaijan and call out the war crimes of
  the Aliyev regime.

  Asatryan reiterated that what is taking place in Artsakh is genocide and stated that all the
  residents of the Glendale sister city of Martuni have been moved out of their homes. She
  stated that here are thousands of families who have become homeless and thousands more
  who are trying to escape to safety. Councilmember Asatryan expressed disappointment in
  the pledge that Samantha Powers had made for humanitarian aid to the refugees from
  Artsakh stating that it was grossly insufficient and insulting. She also mentioned that the
  Azerbaijani government has rounded up all the leaders of the Republic of Artsakh to try
  them and she compare this to the rounding up and execution of all the leaders and
  intellectuals during the 1915 Armenian Genocide. She made a call to the allies of the
  Armenian community to speak up and help with humanitarian efforts. Asatryan spoke about
  her family in Artsakh and the connection that most Armenians have to the impacted families.
  She spoke about the humanitarian campaign that was launched to help the survivors of the
  1915 genocide and made a call for a similar action in the US to address the current
  humanitarian crisis. She invited the public to visit the website
  https://americawethankyou.org/, to learn more about the movement to recognize the
  outpouring of generosity by the American people from the onset of the Armenian Genocide
  (1915-1923).
